promptLatex: Three distinct numbers are placed into three labelled boxes, one number per box, chosen uniformly from all $6$ possible placements. What is the probability that box $1$ receives the largest of the three numbers?
hintLatex: Each of the three numbers is equally likely to land in any of the three boxes.
Fix one of the three numbers. It lands in box $1$ in exactly $2$ of the $6$ placements.
solutionLatex:
The sample space is the $3! = 6$ ways of placing three distinct numbers into three labelled boxes.

Fix the largest of the three numbers. It can be placed in box $1$ first, and then the remaining two numbers can be placed in $2$ orders, giving $2$ placements out of $6$. Equivalently, each number is equally likely to occupy each of the $3$ boxes.

Therefore $P = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$.
